label: Bible Study
prompt: Let us therefore follow after the things which make for _____, and things wherewith one may edify another.
verse: Let us therefore follow after the things which make for peace, and things wherewith one may edify another.
note: Pursue what makes for peace — and what builds each other up.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Having many things to write unto you, I would not write with paper and _____: but I trust to come unto you, and speak face to face, that our joy may be full.
verse: Having many things to write unto you, I would not write with paper and ink: but I trust to come unto you, and speak face to face, that our joy may be full.
note: John would rather visit than write — paper and ink can't beat a face-to-face conversation.

label: Sunday School
prompt: Behold, we put _____ in the horses' mouths, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body.
verse: Behold, we put bits in the horses' mouths, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body.
note: James' tongue lesson: a small bit steers a whole horse — and a small tongue steers a whole life.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou _____ unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.
verse: Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.
note: To persecuted, poor Smyrna, Jesus gives no rebuke at all — only courage and the promise of a crown.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an _____.
verse: But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.
note: Paul's blunt family-finance rule: whoever won't provide for his own household is 'worse than an infidel.'
